summary: Attacked the extraction of Xie–Yuan, 'Geometric Bogomolov conjecture in arbitrary characteristics' (arXiv:2108.09722v1; Invent. Math. 229 (2022)): 65 items, 4 routes, 15 source issues. Ten findings: one high, five medium, four low. The items, locators, library citations, routing and the fifteen recorded mistakes hold. The high finding is a false item. Item good-reduction-model says Zariski closures of abelian subvarieties of a good-reduction abelian variety are abelian subschemes. In characteristic p this fails (an explicit Moret-Bailly α_p example over P¹). The paper's Proposition 5.4 relies on this unproved step, and it should use Néron models instead. Two unrecorded mistakes in §3: the 'bijection' I(K̄/k̄) → I(K/k) in the proof of Proposition 3.6 is not injective, and the claimed equivalence fails. The proof of Proposition 3.2 silently needs k₁, k₂ algebraically independent, which Corollary 3.5(i) does not provide. Theorem 1.1 survives both, by the repairs given. Missing items: the functoriality, product, field-extension and M_K-field comparison properties of ĥ; density of prime-to-p torsion; and the §4 inputs (seesaw, [m] of degree m^{2g}, projectivity and relatively ample rigidified bundles). Low: normality of the pencil model H in Lemma 3.7; Serre multiplicities and associativity against SF.5; a characteristic-0-scoped blow-up owner; and Scanlon missing from the prerequisites.
checked: The source, re-fetched from https://arxiv.org/pdf/2108.09722v1 on 29 September 2026: SHA-256 2587e70314bddb8f2ed01768f64b4a96b5da0f32d0d5382b4336b2415211c2ab, the recorded hash. The unversioned URL serves the same file. The arXiv API lists only v1 (22 August 2021, 29 pages, DOI 10.1007/s00222-022-01112-1). The Springer article page redirects to a cookie wall and serves no PDF. Crossref records no update or relation (licence: TDM only). So, like the extraction and the review, every finding here is scoped to arXiv v1.
The whole paper read in the text layer, §§1–5 and the references, with page images at pp. 13, 16 and 25 (the text layer drops overlines such as k(S_i)‾ = k_i and I(K̄/k̄)).

All 65 items against the paper: statement, hypotheses and locator. Locators were checked page by page for §§2.1–2.3, 3.1–3.3, 4.1–4.3 and 5–5.3. Counts: 4 library, 9 planned, 52 missing. Every missing item is routed exactly once (52 ids, 52 distinct, equal to the missing set). Every planned stage id and every route stage id resolves in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/.

Every library citation, at the pins, from the declarations index and the files. TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety (structure: proper, geometrically integral group object over Spec K; AbelianVariety/Basic.lean:94); .prod (Product.lean:61); .baseChange (Basic.lean:274); .mulBy (End/Basic.lean:243); .IsIsogeny (Isogeny.lean:61, finite and surjective). Mathlib Algebra.trdeg (RingTheory/AlgebraicIndependent/Basic.lean:45), Matrix.IsReducedRowEchelon (LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Echelon/Basic.lean:89), AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicCycle (AlgebraicCycle/Basic.lean:44). TauCeti.isReducedRowEchelon_rowReduceMatrix (LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Echelon/RowReduce.lean:379). All exist and say what the items need. No uniqueness of reduced row echelon form was found in either library.

The missing statuses, by searching declarations.tsv in both libraries for nef, Bertini, blow-up, fibre dimension or semicontinuity, geometrically integral openness, K/k-trace or Lang–Néron, Northcott, Manin–Mumford or Bogomolov, Chow group or rational equivalence, abelian scheme, rigidified or cube, canonical or Néron–Tate height, stabilizer, and intersection multiplicity. The only hits are unrelated (a plumbing-graph blowUp; TauCeti.Order.Northcott for counting norms; WeierstrassCurve canonical heights for elliptic curves, which do not give the items). No missing item is in either library.

Each planned stage in full: RP.5 (translates, stabilizers, Manin–Mumford 'with precise characteristic and field hypotheses', Bogomolov over number fields only), SF.5, MC.0 (numerical equivalence against complementary cycles, which for 1-cycles is the paper's), A3, A6 (Poincaré complete reducibility over fields), R11.1 and R11.3. The characteristic-free generality holds for all of them. The exceptions are finding 1 (R11.1 does not plan closures, and the claim is false) and finding 8 (SF.5 and multiplicities).

Route owners and duplication against the other extractions that route to the same places: PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19 (items 3–6, 11, 20, 68–69, 72), PAPER-YUAN-26, PAPER-GAO-GE-KUHNE-26, PAPER-DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21, PAPER-DEMARCO-KRIEGER-YE-20 and PAPER-DEMARCO-MAVRAKI-YE-26. The function-field heights, the trace and the Néron–Tate kernel go to RP.0/RP.1 as GH19 routes them. Gubler's Cor. 4.4 matches GH19/72 in the same Part II. The Yuan–Zhang fundamental inequality (DMY26/35, ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII) is the number-field adelic version, so it is not a duplicate of this paper's function-field item. The ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights and TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic layers do not plan function-field Bogomolov. No duplicate owner was found beyond the imports named in findings 6 and 9.

The Part II route: every other extraction proposing HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructionsPartII uses area arithmeticgeometry. This route's title matches GH19, GGK26, DGH21, DKY20 and DMY26 (YUAN-26 alone differs). RP.5 is explicitly number-field Bogomolov, so the function-field theorem has no other owner.

The cited inputs at their sources. Yamaki arXiv:1405.0896v5 (SHA-256 0bb02ad9…4b1634), Theorem 1.5 (a)⇔(b)⇔(c) and the definition of nowhere degenerate ('A ⊗_K K̄_v is the generic fiber of an abelian scheme'), which under (c) is good reduction, consistent with the extraction's note. Gubler arXiv:math/0609387v2 (SHA-256 b11dab54…df680): §3.1, Theorem 3.6, Lemma 4.1 and Corollary 4.4. Conrad, Kktrace.pdf (SHA-256 f73508a4…611ec), Theorem 9.15 (positive-definiteness modulo the trace over a generalized global field (V, N)), which with Lang–Néron gives the northcott-trivial-trace item. Scanlon arXiv:math/0303340v1, Theorem 2.2 and its attribution to Pink–Roessler [7], which supports the review's Manin–Mumford note. The arXiv abstract of Pink–Roessler's ICM paper (math/0212408) says it is characteristic 0, as the review says.

All 15 recorded source issues at their locators: E1 (including both counterexamples, and the repair through k_A and Corollary 3.5(ii)), E2, E3 (against Gubler Cor. 4.4), E4, E5 (the two-pencil repair), and the misprints E6–E15 in the text layer. All are correct as recorded. The paper was then read again for unrecorded mistakes, which gives findings 1, 2, 3 and 7.

The review's changes: the fifteen verdicts, and the manin-mumford note (Scanlon's special subvarieties become torsion translates under trivial trace, since a homomorphism from A_K̄ to a group over F̄_p ⊆ k would give a nonzero constant quotient and so a nonzero trace). Its E1 counterexample (a curve C with trivial stabilizer translated by a non-k′-rational point) is correct. Its E13 projection-formula remark is correct: [𝒴]·[ℒ_ℬ]^{e+1} pushes forward to a divisor on 𝒜′. No error was introduced. The one gap is the unrecorded prerequisite in finding 10.
Not done: the Inventiones version was not available, so nothing was collated against it. Lang's Fundamentals, Hrushovski 2001 and Pink–Roessler 2004 were not opened. No Lean was written or run.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22.result.json, item PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/good-reduction-model (its second clause) and the proof note of PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/prop-5-4; the missing sourceIssues entry for the proof of Proposition 5.4
findings.claim: The item says: 'abelian subvarieties of A have Zariski closures that are abelian subschemes', citing the proof of Proposition 5.4, p. 25, and marks it planned at NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.1. As a general statement over a curve in characteristic p this is false. The paper asserts it without proof ('Both 𝒜′ and ℬ are abelian schemes over S') and then applies Proposition 2.1 (which needs smooth projective 𝒜′, ℬ and a flat h), Proposition 4.2 (which needs an abelian scheme 𝒜′) and Lemma 4.1(4) to these closures. The mechanism is that two finite flat subgroups of order p that meet trivially on the generic fibre can coincide on a special fibre, so a homomorphism of abelian schemes can be a closed immersion generically and have kernel α_p at one point; its image, which is the Zariski closure of the generic abelian subvariety, then has a non-reduced special fibre. Neither the extraction nor the review records this step as a source issue. The fifteen recorded issues E1–E15 do not touch it.
findings.evidence: Source: arXiv:2108.09722v1, proof of Proposition 5.4, p. 25, checked on the page image: 'Denote by 𝒜′ (resp. ℬ) the Zariski closure of A′ in 𝒜 (resp. B in 𝒜 ×_S 𝒜). Both 𝒜′ and ℬ are abelian schemes over S.' No argument is given. Counterexample to the item's clause, over S = P¹_k with k algebraically closed of characteristic p. Let E be a supersingular elliptic curve over k and C₀ = E × E, so C₀[F] = α_p × α_p. The α_p-subgroups G_λ = {(at, bt)} for λ = (a:b) ∈ P¹ form a finite flat subgroup scheme G ⊂ C₀ × P¹ of order p; on the chart b = 1 it is Spec O[y]/(y^p) with x = ay (Moret-Bailly's family). Fix λ₀ ∈ P¹(k) and set i = (q₁, q₂) : C₀ × P¹ → A := (C₀ × P¹)/G ×_{P¹} (C₀/G_{λ₀} × P¹). Both factors are abelian schemes over P¹, so A has everywhere good reduction. Over K = k(λ), ker i_K = G_λ ∩ G_{λ₀} = 0 because λ ≠ λ₀, so i_K is a closed immersion and B := i_K(C₀,K) is an abelian subvariety of A_K. At λ₀, ker i_{λ₀} = G_{λ₀} ≅ α_p, and i_{λ₀} has degree p onto its image D. The Zariski closure 𝒳 of B is the scheme-theoretic image of i (C₀ × P¹ is integral and i is proper). Specialization of cycles commutes with proper pushforward (Fulton, Intersection Theory, §20.3), so [𝒳_{λ₀}] = i_{λ₀*}[C₀] = p·[D]. So 𝒳 has a non-reduced fibre at λ₀ and is not smooth over P¹: it is not an abelian scheme. Only non-étale finite subgroup schemes can do this, so this is a characteristic-p phenomenon, which is exactly the generality this paper adds. The example has non-trivial trace, but the item states the clause without that hypothesis. The paper's trivial-trace setting (d)–(e) gives no argument that excludes the same collision at a place of S. The owner R11.1 (research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties.json) plans 'Compare good reduction with an abelian-scheme model' and 'functorial extension of homomorphisms'; it says nothing about Zariski closures of abelian subvarieties.
findings.fix: (1) In good-reduction-model, delete the clause 'abelian subvarieties of A have Zariski closures that are abelian subschemes'. Replace it with: 'an abelian subvariety A′ of A has good reduction, so its Néron model 𝒜′₀ is an abelian scheme over S, and the inclusion extends to a homomorphism 𝒜′₀ → 𝒜 (Néron mapping property); this need not be a closed immersion in characteristic p'. (2) Add sourceIssues entry E16, kind 'gap', locator 'proof of Proposition 5.4, p. 25', printed as quoted above, affects 'the proof', known 'new'. Its correction: replace the Zariski closures by Néron models, namely 𝒜′ := the Néron model of A′ and ℬ := 𝒜 ×_S 𝒜′ (the Néron model of B ≅ A × A′ via (x, z) ↦ (x, z − x)), with h the second projection, which is flat. Take 𝒴 to be the closure of Y in this ℬ. Proposition 2.1, Proposition 4.2 and Lemma 4.1 then apply verbatim, and heights may be computed on any model with a symmetric rigidified extension. Record the counterexample above in the reason. (3) Update the prop-5-4 note and the Part II brief to say 'Néron models of A′ and B' where they now rely on closures.

findings.claim: The first step of the proof of Proposition 3.6 is false as printed. The paper reduces to algebraically closed k and K through the claim that k′ ↦ k′ ∩ K is a bijection φ : I(K̄/k̄) → I(K/k) with 'X special for A_K̄/K̄/k′ iff X special for A/K/φ(k′)'. The map is not injective, and the equivalence fails. Proposition 3.6 is stated for arbitrary K with k algebraically closed in K, and the item copies that statement. So the design job would follow a reduction that does not work. Theorem 1.1 survives: Proposition 3.1 needs only the case where K is algebraically closed, together with the fact that the algebraic closures of two distinct fields k₁, k₂ ∈ I(K/k) of transcendence degree 1 meet in k̄. The general statement is also true by a Galois argument, but that argument is not the paper's.
findings.evidence: Source: arXiv:2108.09722v1, proof of Proposition 3.6, p. 16, checked on the page image: 'There is an bijection φ : I(K̄/k̄) → I(K/k) sending k′ to k′ ∩ K. Because φ preserves the ordering and for k′ ∈ I(K̄/k̄), and X is special for A_K̄/K̄/k′ if and only if X is special for A/K/φ(k′), we may assume that k and K are algebraically closed.' Counterexample. Take K = k(s, t) with k algebraically closed, u = √s + t ∈ K̄, and k′ = the algebraic closure of k(u) in K̄, so k′ ∈ I(K̄/k̄). Let σ ∈ Gal(K̄/K) send √s to −√s, and set u′ = σ(u) = −√s + t. If f ∈ K is algebraic over k(u), then applying σ shows f is algebraic over k(u′). Since u and u′ are algebraically independent over k (they generate k(√s, t)), the algebraic closures of k(u) and k(u′) meet only in k, so f ∈ k. Thus φ(k′) = k′ ∩ K = k = φ(k̄), and φ is not injective. For the equivalence, let A = E_K with E an elliptic curve over k, and X = {P} with P ∈ E(k′) a point with x(P) = u. Then X is special for A_K̄/K̄/k′ (take Y = {P}). It is not special for A/K/k, because that would put P in E(k) + E_tor = E(k).
findings.fix: Add sourceIssues entry E17, kind 'error', locator 'proof of Proposition 3.6, first paragraph, p. 16', printed as quoted, affects 'the proof', known 'new'. Correction: 'Prove the statement for K̄/k̄, giving F := k_{A,X} ∈ I(K̄/k̄). Let F′ be the compositum of the finitely many conjugates σ(F), σ ∈ Aut(K̄/K), and set k_{A,X} := K ∩ (algebraic closure of F′). For k′ ∈ I(K/k), X is special for A/K/k′ iff F ⊆ (k′)‾ iff F′ ⊆ (k′)‾ (the latter is Aut(K̄/K)-stable) iff k_{A,X} ⊆ k′ (since F′ is algebraic over F′ ∩ K^perf, whose p-power-th powers lie in K, and k′ is algebraically closed in K).' In the prop-3-6 item note, say that the printed reduction is replaced by this argument. Also note that Proposition 3.1 needs only the case where K is algebraically closed.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22.result.json, sourceIssues (no entry) and items PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/prop-3-2 and PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/cor-3-5-i
findings.claim: The existence part of the proof of Proposition 3.2 only works when k₁ and k₂ are algebraically independent over k, that is, when trdeg(k₁k₂/k) = trdeg(k₁/k) + trdeg(k₂/k). The statement assumes only k₁ ∩ k₂ = k. The proof picks a flat quasi-finite ψ : U → S₁ × S₂ with k(U) finite over k₁k₂ (after its reduction to K/k₁k₂ finite) and k(S_i) with algebraic closure k_i. Such a ψ exists only when dim U = dim S₁ + dim S₂, and without it the component V of ψ⁻¹(S₁ × s₂) need not dominate S₁, so 'k(V)/k(S₁) is finite' fails. Corollary 3.5(i) applies Proposition 3.2 to k′, k_A over the base k′ ∩ k_A, and these can be algebraically dependent. So Corollary 3.5(i), and with it the existence of k_A used in Proposition 3.6 and in E1's repair, is not proved in general. Proposition 3.1 needs only two distinct subfields of transcendence degree 1. Those are automatically independent, so Theorem 1.1 survives through a direct argument (see the fix). The item prop-3-2 copies the general statement, and nothing records the gap.
findings.evidence: Source: arXiv:2108.09722v1, p. 13 (page image checked): 'For i = 1, 2, there is a k-variety S_i, an abelian scheme π : 𝒜 → S_i such that k(S_i)‾ = k_i … Because A₁ ⊗_{k₁} K ∼ A₂ ⊗_{k₂} K, there is k-variety U satisfying k(U) = K, a flat and quasi-finite morphism ψ : U → S₁ × S₂'. Then p. 14: 'Because k(V)/k(S₁) is finite, taking the geometric generic fibers in (3.1) and (3.2), we get A₁ ∼ A_{s₂} ⊗_k k₁.' Proof of Corollary 3.5, p. 15: 'One may assume that trdeg(k′/k) < ∞. By Proposition 3.2, k′ ∩ k_A ⊆ I [sic, E8].' Here k′ and k_A are arbitrary algebraically closed intermediate fields. The hypothesis k₁ ∩ k₂ = k does not force independence. In K = k(x, y, z)‾, take k₁ = k(x, y)‾ and k₂ = k(z, x + yz)‾. Then trdeg(k₁k₂/k) = 3 < 4. If g ∈ k₁ ∩ k₂ were transcendental over k, some p-power g′ of g (g′ = g in characteristic 0) is separable over both k(x, y) and k(z, x + yz). Then ∂_z g′ = 0, and D g′ = 0 for D = z∂_x − ∂_y, which kills z and x + yz. So z·∂_x g′ = ∂_y g′ with both partials in k(x, y, g′), over which z is transcendental. Hence all k-derivations of k(x, y) kill g′. The same holds for every p-power root of g′, which is again in k₁ ∩ k₂, so g′ is algebraic over k, a contradiction. So k₁ ∩ k₂ = k. The sourceIssues list E1–E15 has no entry on Proposition 3.2 or Corollary 3.5 beyond the misprint E8.
findings.fix: Add sourceIssues entry E18, kind 'gap', locator 'proof of Proposition 3.2, pp. 13–14, as applied in the proof of Corollary 3.5(i), p. 15', affects 'the proof', known 'new'. Its correction should say one of two things. (a) Prove Proposition 3.2 when k₁ and k₂ are algebraically dependent. The fixer must supply the argument; this red team did not settle whether the dependent case holds in characteristic p. (b) Restrict Proposition 3.2 to algebraically independent k₁, k₂. In place of the uses of Corollary 3.5(i) and Proposition 3.6 in Proposition 3.1, prove directly: if X is special for A/K/k₁ and for A/K/k₂, with k₁ ≠ k₂ algebraically closed in K of transcendence degree 1, then X is special for A/K/k. For this, reduce to Stab⁰(X) = 0 and T_X = A as in the proof of Proposition 3.6. E1's argument then gives that A is defined up to isogeny over k₁ and over k₂, and Proposition 3.2 (independent case) gives A ∼ A₀ ⊗ K with A₀ over k. Then Φ(X) is defined over k₁ and over k₂, so over k by Lemma 3.4. Carry the chosen form into items prop-3-2, cor-3-5-i, prop-3-6 and prop-3-1 and into the Part II brief.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22.result.json, items PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/canonical-height, height-quadratic-bound and small-points; route 1 (source → HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.0)
findings.claim: The extraction defines ĥ only through intersection numbers on models, (1.1)–(1.2), and has no item for the properties of ĥ that the proofs use. These are: (i) functoriality under homomorphisms, ĥ_{φ*L} = ĥ_L ∘ φ, together with ĥ of an image under an isogeny; (ii) additivity on products, ĥ_{p₁*L₁+p₂*L₂}(x, y) = ĥ_{L₁}(x) + ĥ_{L₂}(y); (iii) mutual boundedness of ĥ_L and ĥ_{L′} for two symmetric ample bundles, which the small-points item asserts in passing; (iv) behaviour under a finite extension K′/K (the model changes to the normalization S′ of S in K′, and for trdeg 1 heights scale by [K′:K]), which the reductions (c), (e) and §5.1 use each time K is enlarged; (v) the identification of this model height with the Néron–Tate height on K as an M_K-field (places the prime divisors of S, weighted by deg_M). The cited inputs are stated for the height in (v): Conrad's Theorem 9.15 (behind the northcott-trivial-trace item), Yamaki's Theorem 1.5, Gubler's Lemma 4.1 and Corollary 4.4, and Lang's Ch. 6 Thm 5.4. Without these items, Lemma 5.3 and Proposition 5.4 cannot move small points between X, X^r, X_r, B × C and Y ⊂ B, and the imported theorems cannot be applied to the paper's ĥ.
findings.evidence: Source: arXiv:2108.09722v1, proof of Lemma 5.3, p. 24: 'Then its image X′ = B + t′ in A′ contains a dense set of small points of A′/K/k … Choose L = p₁*L₁ + p₂*L₂ … For any point x ∈ B(K̄), we have the heights ĥ_L(x + t′) = ĥ_{L₁}(x) + ĥ_{L₂}(t′)'. Here A → A′ = B × C is an isogeny, so (i)–(ii) are used. Proof of Proposition 5.4, p. 26: '“small points” of X transfer to “small points” of Y = X_{r−1} × X. Then Y has a dense set of small points in B' uses (i)–(iii). §5.1, p. 23, and proof of Lemma 5.3, pp. 23–25: 'By extending K and k if necessary', 'by replacing K by a finite extension', 'we may need to replacing K by a finite extension again' use (iv). For (v): the paper cites [Gub07, Theorem 3.6] for (1.2). In Gubler, arXiv:math/0609387v2, Theorem 3.6 characterizes the Néron–Tate height of subvarieties by '(a) multilinear and symmetric … (b) If ϕ : A′ → A is a homomorphism … ĥ_{ϕ*L₀,…,ϕ*L_d}(X′) = deg(ϕ)ĥ_{L₀,…,L_d}(X) … (d) …', with heights over the M_B-field of §3.1. Conrad (Enseign. Math. 2006, Kktrace.pdf, Theorem 9.15) proves positive-definiteness of ĥ_{K,L} for K 'a structure of generalized global field by means of a pair (V, N) … as in Example 8.4', and Yamaki (arXiv:1405.0896v5, §1.2) uses 'the set {|·|_{v,H}}_{v∈M_K}'. None of the 65 items states (i)–(v). The nearest are canonical-height (existence and independence of the model), height-quadratic-bound and small-points ('any two such heights bound each other', unproved). For comparison, PAPER-DEMARCO-KRIEGER-YE-20/49 has the number-field functoriality as an item (planned RP.0), and PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19/5–6 route the Weil and Néron–Tate heights over the function field of a curve to RP.0.
findings.fix: Add items routed with route 1 to RP.0 as a source. (a) 'Properties of ĥ over a polarized finitely generated K/k' (Gubler 2007, Thm 3.6(a)–(c) and its point case): multilinearity, functoriality under homomorphisms and isogenies, additivity on products, and comparability of ĥ_L and ĥ_{L′} for ample symmetric L, L′. (b) 'Heights under finite extension of K and of the constant field': the normalized model S′, pullback of M, and the scaling of ĥ, with the consequence that dense small points and specialness are unchanged. (c) 'Model heights equal M_K-field Néron–Tate heights' (Gubler 2003, Thm 11.18; Gubler 2007, §3.1 and Thm 3.6(d)), linking to GAO-HABEGGER-19/5–6 for trdeg 1. Then cite (a)–(c) in the notes of lemma-5-3, prop-5-4, reduction-a-d and northcott-trivial-trace.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22.result.json — no item for density of torsion points; used by PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/section-5-3, PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/special-has-small-points and the correction of sourceIssues E2
findings.claim: The §5.3 induction concludes from 'A′(K̄)_tor ∖ A′_{e+1}(K̄) is Zariski dense in A′'. With E2's correction it needs the stronger fact that the torsion points of order prime to char k are Zariski dense in an abelian variety, and hence off any proper closed subset. The same density makes a torsion subvariety have dense small points, which is part of special-has-small-points. No item states it, and E2's correction relies on it without an owner. Neither library has it: Tau Ceti's abelian-variety files have [n] (mulBy) but no torsion results, which the review itself notes ('no trace, torsion-scheme, duality or reducibility results').
findings.evidence: Source: arXiv:2108.09722v1, §5.3, p. 27: 'As A′(K̄)_tor ∖ A′_{e+1}(K̄) is Zariski dense in A′, X_{r−1} × X contains a Zariski dense set of torsion points of A × A.' The extraction's E2 correction says: '§5.3 needs only these: prime-to-p torsion points are Zariski dense in A′, and so are those off the proper closed subset A′_{e+1}.' No item of the 65 states this density (checked by reading all items). Library: TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AbelianVariety/ (Basic, Isogeny, Product, End/, Hom/, MorphismGroup, TangentSpace, Trivial) at f790474 has TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety.mulBy (End/Basic.lean:243) and nothing on A[n] or torsion density. Mathlib 082e2d3 has no abelian-variety torsion API. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A3 plans '[n] is finite locally free of rank n^(2g) … étale precisely under the appropriate invertibility condition' but not density.
findings.fix: Add an item 'Density of prime-to-p torsion': for an abelian variety A over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p ≥ 0, ∪_{(n,p)=1} A[n](K̄) is Zariski dense in A. Proof: its closure is an algebraic subgroup whose identity component C has A/C with only finitely many prime-to-p torsion points, so C = A. Route it to AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3 as a source, next to the rank n^{2g} of [n]. Cite it in section-5-3, special-has-small-points and E2's correction.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22.result.json, items PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/lemma-4-1-1, lemma-4-1-3, prop-4-2 and good-reduction-height; route 3 (source → AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1/A2)
findings.claim: §4 rests on several general facts that no item states and no cited layer plans. (i) The seesaw principle for the abelian scheme π : 𝒜 → S: a line bundle trivial on every fibre is π*N. It is used in Lemma 4.1(1). (ii) A line bundle on 𝒜 trivial on the generic fibre is π*N. It is used in §4.3 to make the extension ℒ automatically symmetric. (iii) [m] on 𝒜 is finite flat of degree m^{2g}, used in the projection-formula computation of Proposition 4.2. Item torsion-part-etale cites A3 only for étaleness. (iv) An abelian scheme over a smooth projective curve is projective and carries a symmetric, relatively ample, rigidified line bundle. This is used in Lemma 4.1(3), in Proposition 5.4 ('Let ℒ_{𝒜′} … be a symmetric, relatively ample and rigidified line bundle') and in feeding 𝒜′, ℬ to Proposition 2.1 as smooth projective varieties. The lemma-4-1-1 note says only 'From the theorem of the cube fibrewise plus the rigidification'.
findings.evidence: Source: arXiv:2108.09722v1, proof of Lemma 4.1(1), p. 20: 'Note that [m]*ℒ − m²ℒ is trivial over every fiber of π : 𝒜 → S, so it lies in π*Pic(S).' §4.3, p. 21: 'In fact, ℒ − [−1]*ℒ is trivial over A, so it is isomorphic to π*M for some line bundle M over S.' Proof of Proposition 4.2, p. 21: '([m]*ℒ)^g · ([m]*ℳ) = deg([m])ℒ^g · ℳ. This is just m^{2g+i}ℒ^g · ℳ = m^{2g}ℒ^g · ℳ.' Atlas: A1 (research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli.json) plans 'rigidity … the theorem of the square and cube', not the seesaw principle. No roadmap in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/ contains the word 'seesaw'. Other extractions own (ii) and (iv): PAPER-DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21/29 'Line bundles trivial on the generic fibre come from the base' (source → SF.0/SF.5) and PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19/14 'Projective presentation of an abelian scheme over a curve' (source → A2). The pinned index (declarations.tsv) has no seesaw, relative ampleness or abelian-scheme declaration in either library.
findings.fix: Add four items and route them as sources. (i) The seesaw principle for a proper flat π with geometrically integral fibres over a reduced base goes to A1 with Lemma 4.1(1). (ii) Trivial on the generic fibre ⇒ from the base goes to SF.0/SF.5, citing DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21/29 as the same statement. (iii) deg[m] = m^{2g} is planned at A3; cite it there. (iv) Projectivity of 𝒜 → S and existence of symmetric, relatively ample, rigidified ℒ go to A2, citing GAO-HABEGGER-19/14. Cite them in the notes of lemma-4-1-1, lemma-4-1-3, prop-4-2 and good-reduction-height.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22.result.json, item PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/lemma-3-7-pencil ('so (H, M_{k′}|_H) is a polarization of K/k′') and sourceIssues (no entry)
findings.claim: §1.1 defines a polarization only over an algebraically closed base field, and it requires the projective model to be normal. Lemma 3.7 calls (H, M_{k′}|_H) 'the polarization … of K/k′' with k′ = k(P¹) not algebraically closed. The proof of Proposition 3.1 then computes heights for K k̄_i / k̄_i with the model H_{k̄_i}. The proof establishes only that H is geometrically integral, never that H (or H_{k̄_i}) is normal. It also never states that the intersection numbers are unchanged by the ground-field extension k_i → k̄_i. The item repeats the unsupported claim. The repair is routine: pass to the normalization, where the pulled-back M_i is still ample and the heights are unchanged by the projection formula. But the formaliser needs it recorded.
findings.evidence: Source: arXiv:2108.09722v1, §1.1, p. 1: 'A projective model of K/k is a normal projective variety S over k with function field K … A polarization of K/k is a pair (S, M) consisting of a projective model S of K/k and an ample line bundle M over S.' Lemma 3.7, p. 17: 'under the polarization (S, M) of K/k and the polarization of (H, M_{k′}|_H) of K/k′'. Proof, p. 17: 'As H₀ is geometrically integral, the generic fiber H′ → Spec k′ of ψ : S̃ → P¹_k is geometrically integral.' Nothing on normality. Proof of Proposition 3.1, p. 18: 'denote by M_i the pull-back of M via (H_i)_{k̄_i} → S. Note that K k̄_i = k̄_i(H_{k̄_i}).'
findings.fix: Add sourceIssues entry E19, kind 'gap', locator 'Lemma 3.7 and the proof of Proposition 3.1, pp. 17–18', affects 'the proof', known 'new'. Correction: 'Let ν : H̃ → H_{k̄_i} be the normalization. Then (H̃, ν*M_i) is a polarization of K k̄_i / k̄_i, and ĥ^{ν*M_i} = ĥ^{M_i} by the projection formula on 𝒜 ×_S H̃, together with invariance of intersection numbers under the flat base change k_i → k̄_i. Alternatively, choose s₀ with H₀ normal as well and use openness of the geometrically normal locus.' In lemma-3-7-pencil, replace 'so (H, M_{k′}|_H) is a polarization of K/k′' by the normalized statement over k̄′.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22.result.json, item PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/intersection-multiplicity (status planned at SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5) and item PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/prop-2-4
findings.claim: The paper defines multiplicities of proper components by Serre's Tor formula. The proof of Proposition 2.4 also uses associativity: the multiplicity of V_i in H₁∩⋯∩H_r∩X equals its multiplicity in (Σ n_j X_j)·H_r, where n_j is the multiplicity of X_j in H₁∩⋯∩H_{r−1}∩X. SF.5's text names Chow groups, Gysin maps and intersection products. It does not name the Tor formula, its agreement with Fulton's multiplicities, or associativity. So 'planned' holds only for the length formula the note mentions, and the associativity step has no item.
findings.evidence: Source: arXiv:2108.09722v1, p. 9: 'Write m(Z, H₁ ∩ ⋯ ∩ H_m ∩ X) for the multiplicity of Z in H₁ ∩ ⋯ ∩ H_m ∩ X, as defined by Serre using the tor-functor.' Proof of Proposition 2.4, p. 10: 'The previous paragraph shows that (Σ n_j X_j) ∩ H_r is a proper intersection and m_i is the multiplicity of V_i in (Σ n_j X_j) ∩ H_r.' SF.5 (research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/SchemeAndStackFoundations.json): 'Construct Chow groups, rational equivalence, proper pushforward, flat/lci pullback, refined Gysin maps, Chern classes and intersection products … Source route. Fulton Intersection Theory'.
findings.fix: Keep intersection-multiplicity at SF.5, but change its note to name what SF.5 must supply. That is: Serre's Tor formula equals Fulton's multiplicity for proper intersections on a smooth variety (Fulton, Prop. 7.1 and §20.4), and associativity of multiplicities for successive Cartier divisors. Mark the Tor-formula comparison and associativity as missing and add them to route 2 as a source.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22.result.json, item PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/pencil-blowup (note) and route 2's reason ('using the blow-ups of AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.7a')
findings.claim: The pencil blow-up must exist in every characteristic. The route builds it on R09.7a, a sub-layer of R09.7, whose stated scope is characteristic 0. It also does not mention that LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.3 already constructs the pencil total space as the blow-up along a smooth axis, which is the special case of this item. So the import is to a layer that does not promise the paper's generality, and it is unclear which layer owns the general pencil blow-up.
findings.evidence: research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry.json, R09.7: 'Its exact scope is varieties of finite type over a characteristic-zero field, with smooth ambient embeddings'. R09.7a: 'Construct blowups by the Rees algebra with their projective universal property'. LPV.3: 'Identify the incidence total space with the blowup along the smooth codimension-two axis'. The paper's use is in every characteristic: arXiv:2108.09722v1, proof of Lemma 3.7, p. 17: 'Let π : S̃ → S be the blowing-up along H₀ ∩ H₁. Then the rational map becomes a flat morphism ψ : S̃ → P¹_k as in [Har77, II, Example 7.17.3].'
findings.fix: In the route-2 reason and the pencil-blowup note, say that the SF.4 blueprint must supply the Rees-algebra blow-up of an arbitrary closed subscheme over any base field, either in SF.4 itself or by confirming that R09.7a's construction is independent of the characteristic. Name LPV.3's smooth-axis pencil as the special case it must agree with.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22.result.json, prerequisites; item PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/manin-mumford (note added by REV-PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22)
findings.claim: The review's note tells the blueprint to derive Theorem 5.1 from Scanlon's Theorem 2.2, the positive-characteristic Manin–Mumford theorem for all torsion, but Scanlon's paper is not in `prerequisites`. The atlas plans no positive-characteristic Manin–Mumford source, so the paper the design is told to follow will not reach a later batch.
findings.evidence: Item manin-mumford note: 'a version covering all torsion, including p-power torsion, is Pink–Roessler … and Scanlon, Positive characteristic Manin–Mumford theorem (arXiv:math/0303340, Theorem 2.2) … the blueprint should derive it that way.' The `prerequisites` list has Yamaki, Hrushovski, Pink–Roessler 2004, Gubler 2007, Gubler 2003, Conrad, Grushevsky–Zakharov, Jia–Shibata–Xie–Zhang, Cantat–Gao–Habegger–Xie and Jouanolou, but not Scanlon. I read arXiv:math/0303340v1 (SHA-256 8e7f3bd8…de44b). Theorem 2.2: 'Let K be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p. Let G be a semiabelian variety over K and X ⊆ G a closed subvariety. Then the Zariski closure of X(K) ∩ G(K)_tor is a finite union of special subvarieties.' Its introduction says 'Pink and Roessler gave an algebraic proof this theorem in [7]'.
findings.fix: Add to prerequisites: T. Scanlon, 'A positive characteristic Manin–Mumford theorem', Compositio Math. 141 (2005), arXiv:math/0303340 (Theorem 2.2 and Definition 2.1), with why: 'the form of Theorem 5.1 for all torsion in characteristic p; with trivial trace its special subvarieties are torsion translates'.
